page: Microsoft Azure B8ls_v2 is a burstable, entry-tier compute instance within the Bsv2 family, configured with 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of system RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, this server type utilizes Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and features 48 MB of L3 cache alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES cryptography. It does not include integrated local disk storage or dedicated graphics processing units, requiring attached remote storage for operational persistence.

Benchmark evaluations position the B8ls_v2 consistently within the middle 50% percentile across general computing workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1638.0 and a multi-core score of 6117.0, paired with an overall PassMark CPU score of 11387.88. Synthetic stress testing demonstrates balanced capabilities, yielding 7752.64 on stress-ng multi-core tests and uncached read memory bandwidth of 59.94 GB/sec. However, data throughput contracts under certain parallel routines, as demonstrated by a weak bottom-25% result of 32.1 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Resource distribution is tailored for burstable access, offering a lean memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This low-memory footprint makes it cost-efficient for intermittent processing demands where continuous sustained compute thresholds are unnecessary. In return, workloads with high memory footprints or heavy concurrent write needs may experience resource constraints under persistent strain.

The hardware configuration is suited for low-to-medium throughput web serving, build automation, continuous integration pipelines, and light background processing. It also handles small-scale Redis caching and lightweight database tasks that do not require massive in-memory storage capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure B8ls_v2 is a burstable virtual machine from the Bsv2 family designed for low-memory, intermittent workloads. Equipped with an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, it provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), and 48 MB of L3 cache. It contains no attached local storage or GPUs, relying on remote storage for disk operations. Benchmark results consistently place it in the average performance tier, registering a PassMark CPU score of 11387.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6117.0, though multi-threaded compression metrics dip into the lower quartile. The B8ls_v2 delivers an economical hardware balance for burst-tolerant applications such as static web serving, CI/CD runners, and light database caching.
